evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper this conflicts on the core spec: it is a Tiptronic, and it is a Cayman S with none of the engine due diligence the profile requires. It also does not serve the accelerated_bridge need or cash preservation.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes to a 2007 Cayman S 3.4, and AutoCheck shows a clean title, no reported accidents and 4 owners. Photos show a clean, apparently stock black car with Sand Beige leather. The dealer text states a 5-speed Tiptronic, which conflicts with the buyer's manual requirement for a keeper. No maintenance evidence is offered at all: no borescope (a hard requirement for any M97 3.4), no DME over-rev report, and no cooling, water pump or AOS records. The $36,985 asking price is above the fair value range of $29,073–$35,848. Close-mileage sold comps sit at $29,500–$34,250, and those include manuals, which command more than Tiptronics. The main open question is cylinder-wall condition, which only a specialist borescope can answer.
evidence.next_action: Ask Casey's Cars in writing whether they will allow an independent Porsche specialist PPI with a full borescope and DME over-rev readout before any deposit, and request the full Carfax/AutoCheck PDFs and any service invoices.
